32	/**
33	 * This produces nearly optimal encodings of text into the first-level of
34	 * encoding used by Aztec code.
35	 *
36	 * It uses a dynamic algorithm.  For each prefix of the string, it determines
37	 * a set of encodings that could lead to this prefix.  We repeatedly add a
38	 * character and generate a new set of optimal encodings until we have read
39	 * through the entire input.
40	 *
41	 * @author Frank Yellin
42	 * @author Rustam Abdullaev
43	 */
44	public final class HighLevelEncoder {
45	
46	  static final String[] MODE_NAMES = {"UPPER", "LOWER", "DIGIT", "MIXED", "PUNCT"};
47	
48	  static final int MODE_UPPER = 0; // 5 bits
49	  static final int MODE_LOWER = 1; // 5 bits
50	  static final int MODE_DIGIT = 2; // 4 bits
51	  static final int MODE_MIXED = 3; // 5 bits
52	  static final int MODE_PUNCT = 4; // 5 bits
53	
54	  // The Latch Table shows, for each pair of Modes, the optimal method for
55	  // getting from one mode to another.  In the worst possible case, this can
56	  // be up to 14 bits.  In the best possible case, we are already there!
57	  // The high half-word of each entry gives the number of bits.
58	  // The low half-word of each entry are the actual bits necessary to change
59	  static final int[][] LATCH_TABLE = {
60	    {
61	      0,
62	      (5 << 16) + 28,              // UPPER -> LOWER
63	      (5 << 16) + 30,              // UPPER -> DIGIT
64	      (5 << 16) + 29,              // UPPER -> MIXED
65	      (10 << 16) + (29 << 5) + 30, // UPPER -> MIXED -> PUNCT
66	    },
67	    {
68	      (9 << 16) + (30 << 4) + 14,  // LOWER -> DIGIT -> UPPER
69	      0,
70	      (5 << 16) + 30,              // LOWER -> DIGIT
71	      (5 << 16) + 29,              // LOWER -> MIXED
72	      (10 << 16) + (29 << 5) + 30, // LOWER -> MIXED -> PUNCT
73	    },
74	    {
75	      (4 << 16) + 14,              // DIGIT -> UPPER
76	      (9 << 16) + (14 << 5) + 28,  // DIGIT -> UPPER -> LOWER
77	      0,
78	      (9 << 16) + (14 << 5) + 29,  // DIGIT -> UPPER -> MIXED
79	      (14 << 16) + (14 << 10) + (29 << 5) + 30,
80	                                   // DIGIT -> UPPER -> MIXED -> PUNCT
